chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about vessels of gold and silver, so he disliked them. I said, 'Some of our companions have narrated that there used to be a mirror for Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) clad in silver?' He said, 'No, and praise be to Allah. It only had a ring of silver, and it is with me.'

Then he said, 'When Al-Abbas was circumcised, a stick clad in silver was made for him, similar to what is made for children, its silver being worth about ten dirhams. So Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) ordered it to be broken.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using gold and silver vessels for eating and drinking in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the distinction between mere adornment and functional extravagance, noting that his silver-clad mirror was only adorned with a silver ring, whereas he ordered the breaking of a fully silver-clad stick given to Al-Abbas for circumcision to prevent ostentation. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *israf* (extravagance) and the practical application of avoiding gold and silver vessels in daily life, even for children, to cultivate humility and distinguish from royal customs.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about vessels of gold and silver. So he<sup>asws</sup> disliked them. So I said, ‘Some of our companions had reported that there used to be a mirror for Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> clad is silver?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! But rather, for it was a ring of silver, and it is in my<sup>asws</sup> possession’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When Al-Abbas was circumcised, a silver-coated stick was made for him, approximately what is normally made for the children, its silver happened to be or approximately ten Dirhams. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> ordered for it to be broken’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘ who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the utensils of gold and silver which he disliked and I then said, ‘It is narrated from certain persons of our people that abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, had a mirror that had a silver covering.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, all praise belongs to Allah. It had only a ring of silver and it is with me.’

He then said, ‘When al- ‘Abbas was circumcised a stick with a silver covering was made for him like things that are made for children. It had about ten dirham of silver and abu al-Hassan, commanded to break it.’”
